root_cause.text: The ctxfi virtual memory allocator was expanded to allocate four device page-table pages (`CT_PTP_NUM=4`) even though `ct_vm_map()` still writes all PTEs only into `vm->ptp[0].area`, causing out-of-bounds access once mappings exceed a single PTP page’s capacity.
root_cause.evidence: The patch says “ct_vm_map() always uses PTEs in vm->ptp[0].area regardless of CT_PTP_NUM” and fixes the crash by reverting `CT_PTP_NUM` from 4 back to 1 in `sound/pci/ctxfi/ctvmem.h`; the CVE description also notes the fault occurs when aggregate allocations exceed the 512-PTE limit of one page.

intent_record.intent_summary: Reduce the device page table page count from four to one to correct the configured memory layout.
intent_record.what: The macro `CT_PTP_NUM`, which defines the number of device page table pages, was changed from `4` to `1`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, any code using `CT_PTP_NUM` will now allocate or assume only one device page table page instead of four, reducing the reserved page table count and changing related memory sizing/initialization behavior.

grouping_result.intent: Reduce the device page table page count from four to one to correct the configured memory layout.

relevance_review.reason: The root cause is a mismatch where the allocator reserves 4 page-table pages but ct_vm_map() writes only into the first one, leading to out-of-bounds access. Reducing CT_PTP_NUM from four to one directly addresses that faulty layout and matches the vulnerability fix.

The root cause is that ct_vm_map() still writes only into vm->ptp[0].area, so expanding CT_PTP_NUM to 4 creates extra page-table pages that are never correctly used and leads to out-of-bounds access when mappings grow beyond one page's capacity.

vuln_statements.stmt_text: #define CT_PTP_NUM	4	/* num of device page table pages */
vuln_statements.explanation: This pre-fix macro expands the allocator to reserve four device page-table pages, but ct_vm_map() still writes PTEs only into vm->ptp[0].area.
